subject: Mythology
title: Anansi in the Americas
description: A 60-second lesson on Anansi in the Americas.

hook.text: Anansi crossed the Atlantic in the minds of enslaved Africans and became the most popular folk hero in the Caribbean.

buildup.text: In Jamaica, Anansi stories taught enslaved people how to outsmart the powerful using cunning instead of force.

discovery.text: Anansi became 'Aunt Nancy' in the American South, evolving into Brer Rabbit — a trickster who outsmarts larger animals.

twist.text: These stories were tools of resistance. A spider outsmarting a tiger taught the enslaved that brains beat strength.

climax.text: Neil Gaiman's Anansi Boys brought the spider god to mainstream fiction, introducing him to millions of new readers.

punchline.text: A West African spider became the voice of resistance across two continents.

quiz.question: How did Anansi stories function for enslaved Africans in the Americas?
options: As religious prayers to maintain their faith
As tools of resistance teaching that cleverness defeats brute strength
As entertainment with no deeper cultural meaning
